summary: Iteration 31 full-stack test of top-10 security fixes + Diretor code-patch apply endpoint. Backend: 9/11 pytest passed, 2 skipped due to register rate-limit 5/hour already exhausted (weak/valid password tests — both verified passing on first pass before rate limit tripped). Frontend: login, WS realtime status 'conectado', Diretor /admin/diretor Aprovadas tab shows aplicar buttons + error retry state, clicking aplicar shows toast and page reloads with acao-aplicacao-erro-{id} + retry button. Logout redirects to /login and revokes JWT (backend confirms /auth/me → 401 'Sessão terminada' after logout).

minor.issue: LLM-generated unified diffs from the security audit consistently fail `git apply --check` (error 'file: No such file or directory' — diffs use only basename like 'mailer.py' instead of 'backend/mailer.py'). Endpoint correctly returns status='falhou' with etapa/erro. Consider auto-prefixing paths or hinting the LLM to include the full repo-relative path in the diff header so approved patches actually apply.

action_items: OPTIONAL: adjust the audit prompt so `diff` fields include the correct file paths ('a/backend/<file>' / 'b/backend/<file>') — currently every applied patch fails and is auto-reverted. Endpoint contract is correct; only patch usefulness is affected.
Cleanup test user created during register test: TEST_iter31_53b9b3@example.com (influencer).
critical_code_review_comments: routes_diretor.py:_apply_patch: tries multiple git-apply strategies but doesn't try `-p1` with a prepended `a/backend/` prefix — could increase success rate for LLM diffs that use file basenames only.

routes_diretor.py:aplicar_correcao does not enforce a lock on double-apply (only checks status=='aplicada'). A second concurrent aplicar on the same 'falhou' action could race — consider setting an intermediate 'a_aplicar' status like `aprovar` does.

core.py:decode_token uses `require: [exp, sub, jti]` — good. But `revoke_token` stores exp as datetime object (jwt.decode without verify_exp still returns exp as int) — actually returns int, so fine. Consider adding a TTL index on `revoked_tokens.exp` so revoked JTIs are auto-purged after 24h.
realtime.py: 8s auth timeout is aggressive if clients are slow; observed working. Consider 10-15s.

The register endpoint's 5/hour IP-based rate limit is very tight for a shared preview environment — testing exhausts it quickly. For prod acceptable; for testing consider raising or exempting internal IPs.
Diretor.jsx line 101 renders `JSON.stringify(a.resultado)` as text — okay for admin, but could look messy for large results; consider a collapsible details block.

success_rate.backend: 100% (9 passed, 2 skipped due to external rate limit)

rca of the issue: N/A — no user-visible bugs. Only observation: applied audit patches always fail because the LLM produces diffs whose --- a/xxx / +++ b/xxx paths are file basenames (e.g. 'a/mailer.py') rather than repo-relative paths ('a/backend/mailer.py'). The apply endpoint tries -p0/-p1/--directory backend but none matches when the header path has no leading directory component and the file is not in repo root. Fix in the audit prompt (routes_diretor.py:_audit_file SYSTEM message) to require full paths, or in _apply_patch add a variant that prepends the area directory to the a/ b/ headers.
